references.text: The leader of the tribe of Judah and the number of men are mentioned again in the organization of the camp.
The second census of the tribe of Judah, showing the change in numbers after the wilderness journey.
Jacob's blessing over Judah, prophesying the tribe's future greatness and leadership.
Judah's birth as Leah's fourth son, the origin of the tribe of Judah.
The tribal inheritance of Judah in the promised land, being the largest and most prominent tribe.
Judah is mentioned in Jesus' genealogy, showing the Messiah's descent from this tribe.
Confirms that the Lord comes from Judah, linking the significance of this tribe to Christ.
The Lion of the tribe of Judah in Revelation, pointing back to the tribe's messianic role.
